label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, D, D where the asset was B, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Against the brief's low, wet, six-legged outline: the body is a low dome, but a long flat snout projects forward about a third of the length (LEFT, RIGHT, FRONT-LEFT), which the brief does not ask for, and the dark spiked crest on the top of the back (FRONT, RIGHT) breaks the smooth low wet outline. The silhouette does not read as the brief's thing.

M2.reason: The brief gives 'the size of a headcrab' but no number, and sizeAsked and sizeOff are null, so no 15% check can be made. Measured 26.4 x 18.1 x 17.6. In lineup.png (C) it is larger than the leech (A) and roach (B) and about the chumtoad's (D) size. Not shown to match, so 1.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: six legs; a ring of teeth around the mouth; a pale belly (paint). Six legs are not clearly there. FRONT and BACK show two legs each, LEFT and RIGHT show two or three per side, and TOP shows two at the front corners; at most four are readable, against six asked. The ring of teeth is there as dark jagged shapes around the underside mouth (BELOW, LEFT), though dark and small. The extra dorsal spikes on the back (RIGHT, FRONT) are not in the brief.

M4.reason: The grey-green body colour matches the brief. The pale belly is missing: BELOW shows the underside as dark brown, and the dark brown patches cover much of the back and flanks (FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT). The brief asks for wet skin and the surface is matte, faceted and flat-shaded, so the material is not wet.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings, but the hard-edged dark brown camouflage-like patches (LEFT, BACK, BELOW) read as stains or paint rather than wet skin, and they add to the wrong look. Not a clear fault of detail sharpness, but not what the brief asks.

M6.reason: Measured on the line-up, as the rubric says, and it caps M6 at 2 here. In lineup.png the asset is C, beside chumtoad (D), roach (B) and leech (A). In the four readings the judges picked chumtoad as not made by Valve in all four, and caught the asset in one (when it was D), so it was taken for one of the game's in three of four.

M7.reason: The brief gives no facing, so the snout is taken as the front. It stands upright on its legs with its underside at the floor line in the walk and leap frames (walk 0/34 to 34/34, jump 0/30 to 30/30), and the mouth reads at the front (FRONT, BELOW).

M8.reason: Triangles are 580, under the limit of 616 (twice the median of Half-Life's own of its kind, 308), so the triangle test passes. SMAK's check is not reported in the measurements (checkErrors is empty). The mouth is open, which a player sees, and the underside is closed in the below view. Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating; the legs reach the floor line in the walk frames.

C1.reason: Through the walk (walk 0/34 to 34/34) and the leap (jump 0/30 to 30/30), the legs stay on the body and the body keeps its low line on the floor. In the leap the legs flail up (jump 17, 21, 26) but do not come apart or float off the body.

C2.reason: Measured: the contract keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts, so it passes.
